The shared csvRow/csvCell helpers in apps/api/src/lib/csv.ts already quote commas per RFC 4180, so the clients export is probably building rows by hand instead of going through them. I'll route it through csvRow, which also gets the formula-injection guard and CRLF line endings for free. Since that changes the customer-facing file, I'll mention it in the PR description.
Action: find the clients table export code, switch it to csvRow/csvCell, and add a test with a company named 'Smith, Jones & Co' that asserts the row keeps the same column count.

The repo pins Node 20.11 in .nvmrc and engines rejects anything else, so the new laptop needs the right Node before install or it will fail with an engines error. It uses pnpm, not yarn.
Action: in ~/code/acme-platform run `nvm install` then `nvm use`, then `pnpm install`, and tell you when deps are in. I'll leave .env.local setup (secrets from your 1Password vault) and the seed run to you or a follow-up.

'Overdue' vs 'Due today' flipping 1 run in 5 smells like the test depends on the real clock or on timezone/date parsing instead of a fixed time. I won't add a retry; I'll make the test deterministic.
Action: open invoice-status.test.tsx and the component it covers, find where 'now' and the due date are computed, pin the clock with fake timers, then run the file repeatedly and under a couple of different TZ values to confirm the flake is gone.

It depends on what the backlog is bound by, and I don't have the numbers yet. Raising concurrency per process is cheap but only helps if the jobs are I/O bound and Postgres/Redis and the email provider can take the extra parallelism; replicas help CPU-bound work and add isolation but cost more connections. I'd rather measure than guess.
Action: look at the worker's concurrency config and queue depth/job duration for the reminder queue, check DB connection headroom, then recommend one with the reasoning.

Easy copy fix plus a test.
Action: grep the web app for 'No invoice yet', change it to 'No invoices yet' and add the missing period to the subtext (checking whether the strings are hardcoded or live in translation files so I update every locale that has them), then update or add a test asserting the new text and run it.

Going ahead with the per-org counter: a new migration `0034_invoice_counters.sql` with a backfill from current max numbers, and an atomic `UPDATE ... RETURNING` in invoice-number.ts scoped by org_id like every other query. The API tests run against a real database via Testcontainers, so I'll confirm Docker is up first.
Action: run `docker info`, write the migration and update invoice-number.ts, then run the api tests in parallel mode to confirm the collisions are gone.

The invoices empty state is InvoicesEmptyState in components/invoices/empty-state.tsx, and web strings go through next-intl, so the copy fix belongs in the message files rather than the component. I'll keep this to the typo and period fix and not fold in the shared EmptyState idea.
Action: fix the English strings in apps/web/messages/en.json, check fr.json and es.json for the same typo, and add a vitest test with plain assertions (toBeTruthy), no jest-dom.

Tailwind here is v4 with CSS-first config in apps/web/app/globals.css, so with next-themes' class strategy the `dark:` variant needs a class-based custom variant declared in CSS, not a tailwind.config.js (none should be created). The badge is probably missing dark styles, or the variant isn't wired to the .dark class.
Action: check globals.css for a `@custom-variant dark` rule and add it if missing, then add dark styling for each status (draft|sent|paid|overdue|void) in InvoiceStatusBadge, using @theme tokens where they exist.

Will do: a responsive 16:9 wrapper around a YouTube iframe with id aB3xK9qLm2Q, with a title for accessibility and lazy loading. I haven't seen how the getting started page or any security headers are set up yet, so I'll check that the embed isn't blocked.
Action: open the getting started page, add the embed component with an aspect-video wrapper, and load the page locally to confirm the video renders without console errors.

Noted: no production deploys on Fridays, and since a v* tag triggers the release.yml prod deploy, no release tags on Fridays either. Today is Thursday, so tagging after lunch is fine; the release run takes about 12 minutes.
Action: find the last v* tag, draft the changelog from the commits since then (grouped by type) in a file for you to review, and not create or push any tag until you say so.

Two separate issues. The build error says a development publishable key is being used in a production build, so the Vercel production environment variable for the auth publishable key is almost certainly set to a dev (test) key; I can't see or change Vercel env vars from here, so you'd need to swap in the live key there. The hydration warning is the due date being formatted in the server's timezone (12:42 PM) and the browser's (8:42 AM).
Action: find the due date column formatting and make server and client render identically (an explicit time zone or a client-side format), and point you to the exact env var to change once I've located where the key is read.

I'll add `memo` as an optional string with a 500-character max to the create-invoice request schema in apps/api/src/schemas using zod, and wire it through the route. The OpenAPI spec is generated from those schemas, so I won't hand-edit the YAML.
Action: update the schema and route/persistence (checking if a DB column or migration is needed), run `pnpm turbo run openapi --filter api` to regenerate apps/api/openapi.yaml, add tests for valid, too-long and omitted memo, and confirm memo appears in the generated spec.

I'll put the signing in apps/web/lib/share-link.ts using Node's crypto HMAC over the invoice id plus expiry, with a constant-time comparison on verify. The signing secret can't be in the client bundle, so if the preview component is a client component it will have to get the link from a server action or route.
Action: look at the preview component and how the web app already reads server-only secrets, then write share-link.ts with sign/verify, wire the copy button to it, and add tests for valid, tampered and expired links; I'll ask you which env var to use if there isn't an obvious one.

The web app is Next.js 15 with the App Router and route groups (marketing), (auth), (dashboard); a reports page for signed-in users belongs in the (dashboard) group, so app/(dashboard)/reports/page.tsx. I'll also leave Marco a comment asking to restore the isActiveMember check, since the failing auth test shows tokens still work after someone leaves an org.
Action: draft the review comment on acme-215-clerk-verify and post it if I have gh access (otherwise give you the text), then scaffold the reports page in the (dashboard) group.

Understood, next-themes with the class strategy: the badge likely has hardcoded light colours or the Tailwind dark variant isn't tied to the .dark class. How to wire that depends on the Tailwind version in use, so I'll check rather than assume.
Action: look at the status badge component and the Tailwind setup (version and how dark is configured), then add dark-mode styles for every status and verify by toggling the theme in the dev server.

I'll use picocolors for the status column: paid green, overdue red, and sensible colours for the other statuses, which I'll take from the actual status values in the invoice type. picocolors turns itself off when output isn't a TTY or NO_COLOR is set, which is good for piping.
Action: find the `invoices list` table rendering in packages/cli, add a status-to-colour helper using picocolors, make sure any machine-readable output path stays uncoloured, and add a small test.

Committing the five fixes to deps/zod-3.24.1 now; typecheck and web tests were already green, and I'll only commit, not push, unless you say so. Then the --json flag for `acme invoices list`.
Action: commit on the zod branch with a message matching the repo's existing style, then add `--json` to the list command that prints the invoices as JSON to stdout (no table, no colour) using the CLI's existing output helper if there is one, with a test.

Before committing I'll make sure the new cli-table3 dependency is in package.json with the lockfile updated, and that the --json path never touches the table or colours. I can't pick the release date for you: I'll leave tagging to you after merge, and it's worth checking what weekday the 9th lands on.
Action: run the CLI tests and typecheck, commit (including the lockfile), push the branch and open the PR, noting that the other commands the audit found without --json (org list, org switch, clients list) are still outstanding.

Setting the Postgres pool max to 10 per pod in apps/api/src/db/client.ts. I'll use whatever option name that driver expects and not change anything else there.
Action: open client.ts, set the pool max to 10, run the api tests, and note in my summary that total connections are pods times 10, so it should stay under the database's connection limit.

The pooler is PgBouncer in transaction mode, so the driver must have prepared statements turned off (`prepare: false`). It's in pool.ts and the options type in driver.ts, but driver.ts doesn't pass it to the raw pool yet, so it's probably still on, which fits the post-deploy errors.
Action: show the one-line change passing `prepare: false` through to the raw pool in driver.ts, and apply it if you want.

Adding an aria-label to the trash button in the line item row; icon-only buttons always need one, so I'll check the other icon-only buttons in that component too.
Action: add a descriptive aria-label (e.g. 'Remove line item', following however the app handles translated strings) to the trash button and any other unlabeled icon-only buttons in that row, add a test that queries by that label, and run the web tests.

So far today:
- Added `maskIban` to apps/web/lib/format.ts (keeps last 4, groups in 4s); 3 tests in format.test.ts pass.
- Started root lint and the full web suite in the background; I haven't seen those results yet.
Action: check the lint and web test results and add them to the list before you paste it into standup notes.

I don't have the pool max per pod in front of me and won't guess a number. Nothing in this session has set it.
Action: read the API's database pool config and deploy settings to find the current per-pod max, then compare pods times that max against the Postgres connection limit to explain the 'too many clients' error and suggest a value.

Sure. I'll write a small TypeScript script in scripts/ that walks each workspace package, counts TODO and FIXME comments, and prints a table with one row per package.
Action: check the workspace layout and how existing scripts in scripts/ are run, write scripts/count-todos.ts (skipping node_modules and build output), run it, and show you the output.

The exports bucket from yesterday is in infra/s3-exports.tf on acme-424-exports-bucket as Terraform, but infra is now Pulumi in TypeScript, so it should go in infra/src/buckets.ts (acme-<env>-exports, private, AES256, 30-day expiry) with the team=payments and env tags via tags(...). I'll only run a preview locally and never apply from a laptop; CI applies.
Action: first confirm apps/api uses Fastify and see how it connects to Redis, write the @fastify/rate-limit plugin (100 req/min per IP, Redis-backed, public endpoints only), port the bucket into buckets.ts, then open the tracking issue with `gh issue create`.

I'll write a browser end-to-end test of that flow against the local dev server: new invoice, pick client, add a line, save, send. I haven't checked yet whether the repo already has a browser test setup or how test data and login work locally.
Action: look for an existing e2e config and fixtures, then write the spec and run it against the dev server.

The existing invoice-reminder job is already idempotent via db.reminderLog.claim(invoiceId, kind, sentOn), so the new queue should send through it and a re-run or redelivery won't double-email customers. The new BullMQ queue also needs removeOnComplete: 1000 and removeOnFail: 5000 like the others, since completed jobs piling up caused the August Redis outage.
Action: read services/worker/src/queues.ts and the invoice-reminder job, add the invoice-reminders queue with those retention settings plus a daily per-org job that finds invoices due in 3 days and enqueues an email for each, and add tests.

Linting and formatting are Biome (`pnpm lint`), so Lena's .eslintrc.json and .prettierrc shouldn't be there. For CORS I'll replace the reflect-any-origin behaviour with an allow-list parsed from the CORS_ORIGINS env var (comma separated, trimmed); anything not on it gets no CORS headers.
Action: check Lena's PR diff and remove those two files, then update the Express CORS setup in apps/api, add tests for allowed, unknown and missing-Origin cases, and run `pnpm lint`.

Adding the YouTube embed (id aB3xK9qLm2Q) in a responsive 16:9 wrapper. The web app sends a CSP on every route, and the headers list frame-ancestors 'none' but I don't see a frame-src, so I'll check whether a YouTube iframe is allowed rather than assume. I'd keep script-src as is.
Action: look at the CSP in apps/web/next.config.ts, add the embed to the getting started page, widen only frame-src for youtube if it's needed, and load the page to confirm the video plays.

On the release: no prod tags on Fridays, so I'll check what weekday the 9th falls on and flag it if it's a Friday.
Action: add the changeset and docs entry, confirm the --json output has no table or colours, run the CLI tests, commit with the lockfile, and open the PR.

Adding a `--json` flag to `acme invoices list` that prints the invoices as JSON on stdout, with no table, colour or extra text so it pipes cleanly into jq.
Action: open the invoices list command in packages/cli, look for an existing JSON output helper to reuse, add the flag and a test that the output parses as JSON, and run the CLI tests.

I'll write scripts/count-todos.ts in the repo's TypeScript style: 2-space indent, single quotes, semicolons, external imports first then local, and ESM `import` only since every package is type: module.

I'll start with the api chart's ExternalSecret and check that POSTHOG_API_KEY is actually listed in its data mapping, and that the deployment consumes that secret. I don't have cluster access confirmed, so I'm starting with the manifests in the repo.

Errors go to Sentry (DSN from SENTRY_DSN) and logging is pino with structured logs, no console.log. So the swallowing catch should log with pino and capture the exception to Sentry, and the job should still fail visibly.
Action: find the catch in the pdf render job, add logger.error with the error and invoice context plus Sentry.captureException, rethrow or mark the job failed, add a test, then commit with a Conventional Commits message like `fix: report pdf render job crashes`.

Adding an aria-label to the trash button in the line item row; icon-only buttons always need one. The branch is already pushed, so I'll add this as a new commit on top and not amend or squash anything.
Action: add a descriptive aria-label to the trash button (and any other unlabeled icon-only buttons in that row), add a test that finds it by label, run the web tests, and commit on top of acme-412-invoice-editor-store.

The likely cause is date handling: dueDate is a plain YYYY-MM-DD, and `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')` parses as UTC midnight, so comparisons against local 'today' flip around the day boundary, especially for your Toronto time. The test also needs a pinned clock instead of the real one.
Action: pin the time with fake timers in invoice-status.test.tsx, parse dueDate as local with `${dueDate}T00:00:00` wherever the status is computed, and run the test under both TZ=America/Toronto and TZ=UTC several times to prove the flake is gone.

This is a bug fix only. I'll keep it out of #1192 and out of the Northwind export request from Dana, which is separate work for another PR. Server CSV goes through csvRow/csvCell, but the current export button builds the CSV client-side, so the duplicate header is likely there.
Action: find the expenses export button, fix the double header, add a regression test asserting the header appears once, and run the web tests.

Adding an optional `memo` (max 500 chars) to POST /v1/invoices. I haven't seen how the API validates requests or produces its docs, so I'll check that before editing anything.
Action: find the create-invoice validation and route, add memo with the 500-character limit, persist and return it (adding a migration if needed), update the API docs the way the repo generates them rather than by hand if they're generated, and add tests for valid, too-long and missing memo.
